_note: The open modality grammar (local-ai-engine.md §4.14). THE LAW ENCODED HERE: (1) inputs are TYPED PARTS — `text` inline, `image`/`audio`/`file` as REFERENCES (a URL, a content handle, a Base file) — and never inline bytes. (2) Outputs are TYPED BLOCKS — `text`, `thinking`, `tool`, `json`, and the reference blocks `audio`, `image`, `file`, `embedding` — where BINARY NEVER RIDES JSON: a reference block carries a loopback or content URL and the native side owns the bytes. This is the voice law of §4.9 generalized to every modality, and it is why a 30-second audio answer does not become a 40 MB base64 string crossing the bridge. (3) The vocabulary is OPEN and versioned: a runtime receiving a block type it has never heard of IGNORES it and SAYS SO with a typed notice — never crashes, never drops it silently. That must-ignore rule is the whole reason a model kind nobody has shipped yet is a data change instead of a refactor. (4) A catalog entry declares its `inputs`/`outputs` from this vocabulary, so a request the model cannot serve is refused typed before the engine is touched.

cases.name: modality: image input rides as a reference part, never as bytes
cases._note: The request that reaches the ABI carries a URL. An implementation that base64s the image into the JSON envelope fails `noInlineBytes`.

cases.name: modality: an audio answer streams as reference blocks
cases._note: Streaming speech: each chunk is a reference the native side already holds, and the loop that plays it never parses PCM out of JSON.

cases.name: modality: a file output is a reference with its type and size
cases._note: Whatever an artifact is, the wire shape is the same: where it lives, what it is, how big. A surface can offer a download without the bytes ever entering the bridge.

cases.name: modality: an embedding is a typed block carrying its provenance
cases._note: Vectors are useless without knowing which model made them at what dimension — the block carries both, which is what Base stores and what makes the drift check in the vector corpus possible.

cases.name: modality: an unknown block type is ignored with a typed notice
cases._note: The must-ignore fixture, and the reason the grammar can grow OTA. A newer engine emits a block this runtime has never heard of: the known blocks still arrive, the request still completes, and the notice records exactly what was dropped so a developer can see it in the log ring rather than guessing.

cases.name: modality: an input the model does not declare is refused before the engine
cases._note: The declared `inputs` list is a contract. Sending an image to a text-only model is answered typed above the seam — no wasted load, no engine-level surprise.

cases.name: modality: a mixed-block answer keeps every block distinct in the snapshot
cases._note: One answer, four kinds of content — the snapshot is an ordered list of typed blocks, not a flattened string, so a renderer can lay out text, a chart and a caption correctly.
